name: Squash and Stretch
visualIdentity: An animation principle rather than a standalone art movement. Objects anticipate, compress or extend at impact, rebound, then settle. Deformation follows movement while preserving apparent volume and recognizable silhouettes; use varied timing and short holds.
suitableUses: Useful when a hero object, logo, character, or word needs a readable moment of physical emphasis. Fits mascot explainers, onboarding loops, title cards, and impact-driven transformations. This suitability is inferred from the source’s examples.
limitations: Avoid deforming every object or leaving elements in continuous wobble. Use only when the scene supports contact, compression, or extension; ambient floating alone is a poor fit. Keep body text legible and contact points coherent. Optional physics does not itself provide fluids, plasticity, tearing, or origami behavior.
palette: Squash and stretch has no intrinsic palette. The supplied four-color example is optional only when task, brand, reference, and existing semantic colors are absent: background #F4EDDF, foreground #32444A, accents #66978E and #C78461. Keep gradients disabled and preserve approved colors, roles, material colors, and any style-specific limits. Accent/foreground pairs fail the stated normal-text contrast target; use the main background for body text and verify actual compositing.
motionAndInteraction: Use explicit pivots, key poses, and controlled scale changes; vary timing, add anticipation and settling holds, and check apparent volume. A uniform spring preset is discouraged. For interactive HTML, possible adaptations include a keyboard-accessible activation that triggers hover, drop, contact squash, and surface growth; bounded pupil tracking where suitable artwork exists; or progress-linked chapter/story states. These are optional patterns, not defining requirements. Reduced-motion and deterministic reverse/direct state behavior matter where applicable.
audio: No fixed soundtrack or mandatory sound is specified. Choose music, voice, effects, ambience, or silence for the topic and audience; restrained impact accents may support contact. Honor supplied audio choices and keep speech clear, levels unclipped, and sound synchronized.
assetRequirements: Provide artwork or geometry with clear silhouettes, pivots, and contact points. Character gaze needs suitable eye layers or a rig; surface growth needs a receiving surface and growth material. Prepare authorized media, fonts, and audio as needed. XPBD simulation is optional and requires a verified solver, defined constraints and fixed stepping; baked or deterministic replay is needed for reliable video seeking.
combinations: Can pair with flat vector character/prop drawing (style-028) for readable silhouettes, or kinetic headline typography (style-093) for a few emphasized words. Keep the four optional palette tokens, deform only the acting element, preserve baseline/contact pivots, and hold settled poses. These combinations are suggestions, not requirements.
productionApproach: Choose the style renderer and motion engine by fidelity and action; SVG and GSAP are recommended for vector poses and seekable motion. Keep one owner per animated property. HyperFrames is the primary composition/export pipeline; use Remotion only if unavailable or a verified limitation blocks a required capability, recording the reason. The pipeline handles assembly, timing, media/audio sync, validation, and export—not the style’s drawing or motion. Drive video from composition time; interactive HTML may use live input. Audio choices and assets remain task-specific.
